channel.title: AI :: FAU Cyber Security Club
channel.description: What language models and agents actually are, how agent systems are built, and why they are both a tool and a target.

item.title: Fundamentals for the AI Era
item.description: What to actually learn now that models write code: the framings worth knowing, the case for small local models, and why the rest of the roadmap matters more.

item.title: Agentic Graphs
item.description: Nodes, edges, state and cycles: the vocabulary for describing systems built from many model calls, the named patterns, and the failure modes.

item.title: Harnesses & the Agent Loop
item.description: What actually turns a language model into an agent: the loop, the harness around it, and the tools people really use.

item.title: Knowledge Bases as Agent Context
item.description: Knowledge graphs against vector retrieval in plain terms, and what document structure actually helps an agent — with this wiki as the worked example.

item.title: AI on Both Sides
item.description: Defensive and offensive application of AI, and the part a cyber club uniquely needs: how agent systems themselves get attacked and defended.
